contentBody: **A new software category solves a problem that most buyers have not yet recognised. Which GTM approach is strongest initially?**
option.1: Prioritise high-intent search terms and minimise educational activity
option.2: Build category awareness while creating routes to capture emerging intent
option.3: Focus on retargeting users who have already reached the pricing page
option.4: Shift spending toward branded search before broadening communication
answerExplanation: Buyers who do not yet recognise the problem need category awareness, and a path ready for intent once it appears.

contentBody: **A company sells ₹40 lakh cybersecurity contracts to a defined list of 600 enterprises. Which channel logic is most appropriate?**
option.1: Maximise broad consumer reach before introducing direct seller engagement
option.2: Prioritise mass social reach because larger audiences reduce acquisition risk
option.3: Combine targeted media, account content and personalised sales outreach
option.4: Use only search because active intent eliminates the need for nurturing
answerExplanation: A defined list of 600 enterprises buying ₹40 lakh contracts is reached through targeted media, account content, and personal outreach.

contentBody: **A campaign receives strong social engagement but very few qualified buyers. Which diagnosis should be tested first?**
option.1: The channel may generate attention without sufficiently matching buying intent
option.2: The campaign necessarily requires more reach before conversions can emerge
option.3: The brand should remove qualification criteria to increase downstream volume
option.4: The same creative should be transferred unchanged to high-intent channels
answerExplanation: Strong engagement with few qualified buyers is a sign the channel is creating attention that does not match buying intent.

contentBody: **When assessing whether WhatsApp belongs in a GTM plan, which factor is most strategically relevant?**
option.1: Whether competitors currently use WhatsApp as part of their marketing mix
option.2: Whether the audience permits direct contact and the interaction adds value
option.3: Whether WhatsApp offers lower CPM than every available advertising platform
option.4: Whether the brand can replace email and sales calls entirely with messaging
answerExplanation: WhatsApp belongs when the audience accepts direct contact and the interaction itself adds value.

contentBody: **What is the strongest purpose of asking AI to critique an AI-generated GTM snapshot?**
option.1: To obtain a second output without requiring additional customer information
option.2: To replace channel testing with a more detailed strategic recommendation
option.3: To expose assumptions, contradictions and gaps before resources are committed
option.4: To ensure the final GTM plan contains every possible marketing channel
answerExplanation: The critique is meant to surface assumptions, contradictions, and gaps before money and effort are committed.

contentBody: **A premium B2B SaaS company receives many Google leads but sales says most buyers are too small. What should the marketer investigate first?**
option.1: Whether keyword intent and qualification criteria match the intended segment
option.2: Whether social reach is large enough to compensate for lead-quality weakness
option.3: Whether the sales team can contact every lead within a shorter response window
option.4: Whether lowering the product price would make existing leads financially viable
answerExplanation: Leads that are too small for the intended segment point first to keyword intent and the qualification criteria.

contentBody: **A brand's target customers spend significant time on Instagram but rarely search for its unfamiliar product category. What is the strongest initial role for Instagram?**
option.1: Capture existing bottom-funnel intent from buyers comparing specific suppliers
option.2: Generate problem awareness and create interest before active search develops
option.3: Replace all performance channels because audience presence proves purchase intent
option.4: Handle product qualification through long-form personalised sales conversations
answerExplanation: When the category is unfamiliar and people are not searching, Instagram's first job is to create the problem and the interest.

option.2: One documenting audience, proposition, channel roles, actions and success measures
option.3: One containing every possible channel so the team avoids missing opportunities
option.4: One focusing entirely on revenue targets without intermediate success indicators
answerExplanation: A strong snapshot records the audience, the proposition, each channel's role, the actions, and how success is measured.

contentBody: **A campaign produces strong awareness but few users later enter consideration. What should the team investigate first?**
option.1: Whether awareness messaging creates relevance and a logical next customer action
option.2: Whether decision-stage discounts can compensate for weak mid-funnel engagement
option.3: Whether total impressions should increase before judging consideration behaviour
option.4: Whether acquisition reporting should exclude users who did not convert immediately
answerExplanation: Awareness that does not become consideration should be checked for relevance and a clear next step for the customer.

contentBody: **A SaaS campaign generates many qualified trials, but most users stop using the product within two weeks. Which metric deserves greater attention?**
option.1: Impression frequency among people who have never visited the product website
option.2: Activation and early usage behaviour among newly acquired trial customers
option.3: Click-through rate for awareness advertisements during the initial launch period
option.4: Search impression share for high-intent keywords used before the trial begins
answerExplanation: Trials that stop within two weeks are an activation and early-usage question, which acquisition impressions do not answer.

contentBody: **Why should campaign messaging change between awareness and decision stages?**
option.1: Each stage represents different customer questions, information needs and perceived risks
option.2: Each stage requires a completely different brand positioning and customer segment
option.3: Decision-stage buyers respond only to price while awareness buyers respond to emotion
option.4: Awareness communication should avoid product benefits until every customer knows the brand
answerExplanation: The message changes because the customer's question, the information they need, and the risk they feel are different at each stage.

contentBody: **A team launches paid media before tracking, landing pages and lead routing are fully ready. What is the main strategic risk?**
option.1: Initial demand may arrive before the system can capture, measure and process it effectively
option.2: Media platforms will permanently penalise the brand for changing campaign settings later
option.3: Awareness activity will always generate lower conversion than campaigns launched after sales
option.4: Customer acquisition cost becomes impossible to improve after the first week of campaigning
answerExplanation: Paid media before tracking, landing pages, and lead routing means demand can arrive before the team can capture, measure, and handle it.

contentBody: **Campaign X has lower CAC than Campaign Y but far worse repeat purchase and retention. What is the strongest conclusion?**
option.1: Campaign X is superior because acquisition efficiency should dominate campaign evaluation
option.2: Campaign Y is superior because retention should always outweigh acquisition efficiency
option.3: Neither can be judged properly without considering downstream customer economics and value
option.4: Both campaigns are equally effective because different funnel metrics cannot be compared
answerExplanation: A lower acquisition cost with worse repeat purchase and retention cannot be judged without the value of the customers who stay.

contentBody: **Traffic to a product page increases sharply, but add-to-cart behaviour remains unchanged. Which interpretation is strongest?**
option.1: Upper-funnel activity is succeeding, so the campaign should scale without other changes
option.2: Additional visitors are arriving, but product relevance or persuasion may remain weak
option.3: Purchase intent is improving because traffic growth normally precedes cart growth
option.4: Awareness frequency is too low because product-page visits should always create cart activity
answerExplanation: More product-page visits with the same add-to-cart rate means people are arriving, while relevance or persuasion is still weak.

contentBody: **Why should a launch plan use different success metrics than ongoing marketing?**
option.1: Because the buyer is the same person so the numbers must match exactly
option.2: Because launch is time-bound first traction, while ongoing is retention and lifetime value
option.3: Because launch should use churn while ongoing never uses churn
option.4: Because ongoing marketing never needs any acquisition metrics at all
answerExplanation: Launch chases first traction; ongoing work is judged on retention and lifetime value.

contentBody: **Which pair best contrasts launch metrics with ongoing metrics?**
option.1: Launch: vanity impressions only. Ongoing: vanity impressions on another app.
option.2: Launch: total ad spend only. Ongoing: total ad spend in email only.
option.3: Launch: day-one signups and press coverage. Ongoing: repeat purchase rate, retention, and churn.
option.4: Launch: follower count only. Ongoing: follower count in a second city.
answerExplanation: Launch tracks the opening spike; ongoing tracks whether the customer relationship pays off.
